solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Closest friend holding a wee creature

indicators.note: the friend word is said to hold the next piece, so it wraps round it

parts.note: a bestie is slang for one's best friend

explanation.surface: A best friend cradles a tiny animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts A inside BESTIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Beastie is a Scottish, affectionate word for a small animal or insect.

clue.text: Oppose note from America

definitions.meaning: to ... a trend is to resist it
US slang for a dollar bill, a banknote

explanation.surface: Objecting to an American message.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucking means going against; a dollar note is called a buck in the US.

clue.text: Piano dropped by biased craftsman

indicators.note: the letter is let go from the following word, so it is deleted

parts.note: partisan means prejudiced in favour of one side
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A prejudiced craftsman gives up a keyboard instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped by' removes P from PARTISAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An artisan is a skilled manual worker who makes things by hand.

clue.text: Note thrilling sensation when removing lingerie, primarily

indicators.note: this letter is taken out of the sensation word

parts.note: a tingle is a thrill of excitement

indicators.note: primarily points to the first letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A frisson as underwear comes off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' gives L from lingerie; 'when removing' deletes it from TINGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinge is a slight trace, as a note of sadness is a hint of it.

clue.text: Drink lager and rye cocktail

indicators.note: a cocktail mixes things together, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A mixed drink of beer and rye whiskey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' rearranges LAGERRYE.
explanation.definitionFit: Earl Grey is a tea flavoured with bergamot oil, a popular hot beverage.

clue.text: Used to running around university, being obedient

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the next piece, enclosing it
running suggests the letters of the two words are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone accustomed to dashing about campus is dutiful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' rearranges USEDTO into DUTEOS, and 'around' puts U inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Duteous is an old-fashioned synonym of dutiful, doing what one is told.

clue.text: Rather dark around hospital boat

indicators.note: the dark word goes around the next piece

parts.note: dingy means gloomy and drab
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A gloomy hospital setting, then a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts H inside DINGY.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinghy is a small open sailing or rowing boat.

clue.text: Check light fixture

parts.note: to test is to check
a match is something to light a fire with

explanation.surface: Inspecting a light fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixture' is a scheduled sporting event, not a fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A Test match is an international cricket or rugby game, a sporting fixture.

clue.text: Boring instructions to stop something squeaking?

definitions.meaning: a boring, a hole drilled into the ground
read as an order, oil it well and it will not squeak

explanation.surface: Dull directions for silencing a creaky hinge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' is a noun, a drilled shaft, not 'dull'.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil well is a shaft drilled into rock to extract petroleum.

clue.text: Wake drunk master after beer is turned over

indicators.note: the shuffled letters come after the beer piece
turning the beer word over reads it backwards

parts.note: pils is short for pilsner, a pale lager

indicators.note: being drunk leaves the letters jumbled

explanation.surface: An intoxicated master after a beer is knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wake' is the noun, the trail behind a moving thing, not the verb; 'turned over' reverses the beer and 'drunk' scrambles master, placed 'after'.
explanation.definitionFit: A slipstream is the current of air or water behind a moving vehicle, like a ship's wake.

clue.text: What a batsman might do: leave

definitions.meaning: in cricket a batsman may play a cut shot and then run between the wickets

explanation.surface: A cricket observation, then a terse instruction to go.
explanation.walkthrough: A cut is a cricket stroke hitting the ball square on the off side; the batsman may then run.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to depart in a hurry, abandoning a situation.

clue.text: Animal's head removed from meat stew

indicators.note: this letter is taken out of the sausage word

parts.note: salami is a cured meat sausage

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cook beheads a beast to make a meat stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' takes A from Animal's; 'removed from' deletes it from SALAMI.
explanation.definitionFit: A salmi is a rich ragout, typically of game birds, partly roasted then stewed.

clue.text: Tools from bushwhackers according to Spooner

indicators.note: Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words

parts.note: fancifully, the bush in bushwhackers is a hedge
fancifully, the whackers in bushwhackers are slammers, people who slam things

explanation.surface: Tools taken from backwoods guerrillas, as the reverend might put it.
explanation.walkthrough: HEDGE SLAMMERS with the initial H and SL exchanged gives SLEDGE HAMMERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sledgehammers are heavy long-handled hammers, a kind of tool.

clue.text: Crudely chide dusty Greek historian

indicators.note: done crudely, the letters are roughly reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Telling off a dusty old Greek scholar rudely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crudely' rearranges CHIDEDUSTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Thucydides wrote the history of the Peloponnesian War in the fifth century BC.

clue.text: Ultimately, boozing in German city results in this?

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the city name

parts.note: Hanover is a city in Lower Saxony, Germany

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A night of heavy drinking in a German city leads to this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' gives G from boozing; 'in' puts it inside HANOVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy drinking produces a hangover, the headache and nausea of the morning after.

clue.text: Too far into the water

definitions.meaning: over the side of a ship

explanation.surface: Pushed too far out into the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Going overboard is overdoing things; falling overboard puts you in the sea.

clue.text: Older bit of stationery lacks power

indicators.note: the stationery item is missing a letter, so it is deleted

parts.note: a stapler is a piece of office stationery
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A desk item without a power supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacks' removes P from STAPLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Staler means less fresh, having been around longer.

clue.text: One very happy to skip end of dance, being lonely

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
so means very, as in so good

indicators.note: skipping a letter leaves it out

parts.note: elated means very happy

indicators.note: end of points to the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled to sit out the last dance, though alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' takes E from dance; 'to skip' deletes it from ELATED, leaving LATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolated means cut off from others, solitary.

clue.text: Nick's more fashionable

definitions.meaning: nick and ... are both British slang for prison; 's stands for is
... as the comparative of cool, trendy

explanation.surface: Someone called Nick is trendier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' is not a name but British slang for a prison, as is cooler.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooler is slang for a jail; cool means stylish, so cooler is more stylish.

clue.text: Once holds top of five iron wrong

indicators.note: the first word holds the following pieces within it
in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A golfer once hit a five iron badly.
explanation.walkthrough: The golf picture misleads: 'iron' is the chemical element, 'top of' picks the first letter of five, and 'holds' puts both inside once.
explanation.definitionFit: An offence is a crime or wrongdoing, a wrong in law.

clue.text: Tequilas, then I am hiding fatigue

indicators.note: the phrase conceals the answer within its run of letters

explanation.surface: A drinker confesses that the tequila is masking tiredness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding' finds the word spanning tequilAS THEN I Am.
explanation.definitionFit: Asthenia is the medical term for abnormal weakness or lack of energy.

clue.text: Rock group's vehicle caught in terrible rain

definitions.note: the definition carries 's, read as 'is', so the band itself is meant

indicators.note: the vehicle is trapped inside the scrambled letters
something terrible is in a bad state, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: a van is a road vehicle

explanation.surface: A band's tour van stuck in a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' scrambles rain into NIRA; 'caught in' places the vehicle within. The definition's 's reads as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nirvana were the Seattle grunge band fronted by Kurt Cobain.

clue.text: Spot the lady's instrument

parts.note: zit is slang for a pimple
her is the possessive for a woman

explanation.surface: Spotting a woman's musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A zither is a flat stringed instrument played horizontally, plucked with fingers.

clue.text: Forbid literal translation: it'll shock you

indicators.note: translating changes the form of words, here rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: A ban on word-for-word rendering comes as a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation' rearranges FORBIDLITERAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A defibrillator delivers an electric shock to restore a normal heart rhythm.

clue.text: Hawk grabs river fish

indicators.note: the hawking word grabs the next piece, holding it inside

parts.note: to hawk goods is to tout them

explanation.surface: A bird of prey seizes a fish from the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hawk' is the verb, to peddle, not the bird; 'grabs' puts R inside TOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A trout is a freshwater game fish of the salmon family.

clue.text: After party, kiss Yankee's ancient mistress

indicators.note: the kiss and Yankee come after the party

parts.note: a do is a party
X is the conventional written kiss
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Following a party, an American kisses his old lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Doxy is an archaic word for a lover or a woman of loose morals.

clue.text: An inclination to back Italian lady

indicators.note: putting the pieces back means reading them backwards

parts.note: a nod is an inclination of the head

explanation.surface: A tendency to support an Italian woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to back' turns ANNOD round.
explanation.definitionFit: Donna is the Italian word for woman or lady.

clue.text: Northern delicacy, to include a thing no-one wants

indicators.note: the preceding letters are made to contain the next piece

parts.note: Lancashire hotpot is a lamb and potato stew from northern England
taken as written

explanation.surface: A northern dish that includes something nobody wants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'include' puts A inside the two pieces. Lancashire hotpot is a slow-baked lamb stew topped with sliced potato, from north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot potato is an awkward issue that everyone tries to pass on.

clue.text: Modest southern bank, perhaps

parts.note: a bank is one example of a lender

explanation.surface: A small bank in the south, maybe.
explanation.definitionFit: Slender means slight or small, as in slender means or a slender chance.

clue.text: Short song about an aromatic plant

indicators.note: the song word goes about, surrounding, the next piece

parts.note: a ditty is a short simple song

explanation.surface: A brief tune about a fragrant herb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' here is the containment signal, not 'concerning'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dittany is an aromatic herb of the mint family from Crete.
